cards.title: A suspicious undertaker invented the automated telephone switchboard
cards.body: In 1889, undertaker Almon Brown Strowger noticed his funeral business was mysteriously drying up. Suspecting the local telephone operator—who happened to be married to a competing undertaker—was redirecting grieving callers to her husband, Strowger designed an electromechanical switch that let callers dial numbers directly without human intermediaries. His automated Strowger switch eliminated operator bias and served as the backbone of global telecommunications networks for nearly a century.

cards.title: A 14-year-old conceived electronic television while plowing a farm
cards.body: In 1921, 14-year-old Philo Farnsworth was plowing a potato field in Idaho when he looked back at the parallel rows of tilled soil. He realized an electron beam could reproduce images the exact same way: sweeping back and forth across a screen, row by row, fast enough that the human eye blends them into a continuous moving picture. Six years later, his raster-scanning concept successfully transmitted the world's first all-electronic television image.

sources.title: Today in History - August 19: Philo T. Farnsworth

cards.title: A wrong resistor in a circuit box created the implantable pacemaker
cards.body: In 1958, American engineer Wilson Greatbatch was building an electronic oscillator to record human heart sounds at the University of Buffalo. Reaching into a tackle box of parts, he accidentally grabbed a 1-megohm resistor instead of a 10,000-ohm one. Installed in the circuit, it pulsed electricity for 1.8 milliseconds and paused for a second before pulsing again—a rhythmic beat that perfectly mimicked a human heartbeat and inspired the first practical implantable cardiac pacemaker.

cards.title: 'Wi-Fi' does not stand for Wireless Fidelity
cards.body: Contrary to popular belief, 'Wi-Fi' is not an acronym for 'Wireless Fidelity' or anything else. In 1999, the Wireless Ethernet Compatibility Alliance hired commercial branding firm Interbrand to replace their unwieldy technical standard name, 'IEEE 802.11b Direct Sequence.' Interbrand proposed Wi-Fi as a catchy, consumer-friendly play on 'hi-fi.' The alliance later briefly used the marketing tagline 'The Standard for Wireless Fidelity' to help consumers understand the technology, creating a decades-long myth.

cards.title: The world's fastest supercomputer was curved to beat the speed of light
cards.body: When Seymour Cray designed the Cray-1 supercomputer in 1975, electrical signals traveled through copper wiring at roughly 20 centimeters per nanosecond. To run at a record 80 megahertz, no wire connecting internal components could exceed four feet in length. Cray bent the entire mainframe into a 6.5-foot-wide C-shaped horseshoe. The inward curve drastically shortened the physical distance between circuit modules, keeping propagation delays low enough to make it the fastest machine on Earth.

quizzes.question: Why did undertaker Almon Strowger invent the automated telephone switchboard?
options: He wanted to reduce long-distance telegraph costs
He suspected a local operator was routing funeral calls to her husband
Human switchboard operators frequently went on strike
The phone company refused to connect commercial storefronts
quizzes.explanation: Strowger suspected a switchboard operator married to his competitor was stealing his funeral business, prompting him to invent direct-dial switching.

quizzes.question: What everyday sight inspired Philo Farnsworth's breakthrough concept for electronic television?
options: The parallel rows of a plowed farm field
The back-and-forth motion of typewriter hammers
The interlocking threads of a textile loom
Sunlight shining through window blinds
quizzes.explanation: At age 14, Farnsworth realized an electron beam could trace an image line by line, just like the parallel furrows of a plowed field.

quizzes.question: What mistake led Wilson Greatbatch to invent the practical implantable cardiac pacemaker?
options: He wired a battery backwards into an amplifier
He dropped a hot soldering iron onto a transistor
He grabbed a resistor with 100 times the intended resistance
He accidentally exposed a circuit to liquid nitrogen
quizzes.explanation: Greatbatch grabbed a 1-megohm resistor instead of a 10,000-ohm resistor, creating an oscillator circuit that pulsed in the rhythm of a heartbeat.

quizzes.question: What does the term 'Wi-Fi' officially stand for?
options: Wireless Fidelity
Wireless Frequency Interface
Wide-Field Internet
Nothing, as it is not an acronym
quizzes.explanation: 'Wi-Fi' was created by a branding firm as a catchy consumer name playing on 'hi-fi' and was never an acronym for Wireless Fidelity.

quizzes.question: Why was the Cray-1 supercomputer designed in the shape of a curved letter 'C'?
options: To allow Seymour Cray to leave his alphabetical initial on the design
To create a natural chimney effect for cooling fans
To keep wire lengths between circuit boards under four feet
To ensure all maintenance panels could be reached from one rolling chair
quizzes.explanation: Electrical signals could only travel about 20 cm per nanosecond, so curving the chassis kept all wiring under four feet to hit 80 MHz speeds.

guesses.prompt: How old was Philo Farnsworth when he conceived the line-by-line scanning idea behind electronic television?
guesses.explanation: Farnsworth conceived the raster-scanning principle in 1921 while plowing a farm field at just 14 years old.

guesses.prompt: To prevent speed-of-light signal delays in the 1975 Cray-1 supercomputer, what was the maximum length allowed for any wire?
guesses.explanation: Because signals travel roughly 20 centimeters per nanosecond, Cray kept every connecting wire under four feet.

misconceptions.claim: The term 'Wi-Fi' is an acronym that stands for 'Wireless Fidelity'.
misconceptions.explanation: Wi-Fi was invented by branding firm Interbrand simply as a catchy name; it was never an official acronym for anything.

misconceptions.claim: Automated telephone switching was invented by telecom engineers seeking to lower corporate operating costs.
misconceptions.explanation: It was invented by undertaker Almon Strowger to stop a biased operator from redirecting his prospective customers to her husband.
